ios.desc:
See every plane overhead in real-time with AR

Point your iPhone at the sky and SkySpottr instantly overlays live flight information on aircraft as they fly by. See callsigns, aircraft types, altitude, speed, and destinations in real-time through your camera.

What You Get:
• AR Camera View - Point and identify any plane overhead instantly
• Real-Time Tracking - Live updates as aircraft move through the sky
• Detailed Flight Info - Callsign, aircraft type, airline, altitude, speed, heading
• Interactive Map - Pan and explore all aircraft in your area
• Spotting History - Keep a personal log of every plane you've spotted
• Favorite Aircraft - Get alerts when specific planes or types fly nearby
• GPS/Location debug - view information about your iPhone's location accuracy + device orientation

Perfect For:
- Aviation enthusiasts curious about overhead traffic
- Plane spotters building their collection
- Anyone who looks up and wonders "what plane is that?"
- Learning about different aircraft and flight routes

How It Works:
SkySpottr uses live ADS-B flight data combined with your location and device orientation to pinpoint aircraft positions with precision. Just open the app, point your camera, and tap any plane to see its details.

Free Features:
- Track 5 nearest aircraft
- 7-day spotting history
- Basic flight information

Upgrade to SkySpottr Pro for:
- Aircraft route info + full location trace
- Unlimited aircraft tracking
- Extended spotting history

show_hn.title: Show HN: I vibe-coded an aircraft AR tracking app and wasted weeks on AI bugs

quotes.text:
Built an app entirely with Claude/AI assistance – backend (Django + C#), iOS frontend, server deployment, CI/CD pipeline, the works. Hosted on a single VPS. Postgres on VPS, Redis on VPS, Django on VPS, etc. The VPS is a VM I have in a proxmox server I have sitting in a datacenter (Dell R630, 1x Xeon 2697v4, 128GB memory, 6x 960GB Intel D3-S4610 with Optane SLOG, etc). No AWS/GCP/Vercel, etc. Incremental cost to me = $0/month. I skipped using CloudFlare tunnels for this - hoping I don't regret that.

What it does: Point your phone at the sky, see real-time aircraft info overlaid on your camera. ADS-B data from community feeders, WebSocket streaming, kinematic prediction to smooth positions between updates. No ARKit – just AVFoundation camera + CoreLocation/CoreMotion + math. SwiftUI overlays positioned via GPS/heading projection.

The humbling part: Spent 2 months debugging "FOV calibration issues." Built an 800-line calibration UI, a Flask debug server, Jupyter notebooks for pipeline analysis, extensive logging infrastructure. Hung a literal picture on the wall with a black rectangle of specific size to "calibrate" the FOV reported by my phone. The AI helped me build all of it beautifully.

The actual bug? A UI scale factor on the overlay boxes. Not FOV math. Not coordinate projection. Just scaleEffect() making things the wrong size. Commit message when I found it: "scale may have been fucking me over for a long time for 'fov issues'". Guess where the scaleEffect() function …
